title: VITALITY Study: Use of Intermittent Hypoxia-Hyperoxia Training (IHHT) for the Reduction of Fatigue in Cancer Survivors – a randomised controlled trial
summary:
VITALITY Study: New Energy After Cancer
Background and Objective of the Study
Many people suffer from persistent and distressing exhaustion, known as fatigue, long after surviving cancer. Conventional methods often provide only limited relief. In the VITALITY study, we are investigating whether a special form of breathing training – Intermittent Hypoxia-Hyperoxia Training (IHHT) – can alleviate this fatigue and improve physical performance.

What is IHHT?
The training works similarly to altitude training for athletes but takes place while relaxing in a seated or lying position. Through a breathing mask, participants alternately receive air with less oxygen (hypoxia) and air with more oxygen (hyperoxia).

Study Procedure

Duration: Participants complete two 45-minute sessions per week over a period of eight weeks.

Comparison: To precisely test the effectiveness, the training group is compared to a control group (a waitlist group that receives IHHT after the study period). Assignment to the groups is done randomly (similar to a lottery).

Assessments: Before and after the training period, we measure fatigue using questionnaires as well as physical fitness (e.g., via a walking test and handgrip strength measurement). We also monitor heart rate variability to see how the nervous system recovers.

Goal of the Investigation
We aim to determine whether this innovative training is an effective and safe method to help cancer survivors gain more quality of life and energy in their daily lives.

interventions.name:
Intermittent Hypoxia-Hyperoxia Training (IHHT)
The intervention consists of two sessions per week, each lasting 45 minutes. Each session comprises 6–8 cycles of alternating oxygen concentrations.

Protocol Details:
- Hypoxic phase: 2–7 minutes per cycle with a fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Cancer survivors defined as (hemato-)oncological patients in follow-up care ≥ 6 months after completion of tumor-directed therapy* with no evidence of disease recurrence. (*Ongoing antihormonal therapy (aromatase inhibitors, tamoxifen) or CDK4/6 inhibitors are not excluded.)
- Fatigue score ≥ 4 on a numerical rating scale (NRS, 0–10).
- Age ≥ 18 years.
- Access to the internet as well as a PC, laptop, or tablet.
- Proficiency in the German language (written and spoken).
- Willingness to participate in an IHHT study / signed informed consent.
- ECOG Performance Status 0–2.
Exclusion criteria:
- History of hypoxia intolerance.
- Resting hypoxemia (SpO2 <90%).
- Anemia ≥ CTCAE Grade 1 (<10 g/dL) or blood transfusion within the last four weeks.
- Sickle cell anemia.
- Inadequately controlled diabetes mellitus.
- Known, unstable thyroid disease, particularly hypothyroidism.
- Instable coronary heart disease.
- Uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia.
- Uncontrolled arterial hypertension.
- Recent myocardial infarction or stroke (<3 months).
- Aortocoronary bypass surgery (CABG) (<3 months).
- Epilepsy or other seizure disorders.
- Severe migraine with aura.
- Increased intracranial pressure.
- Advanced non-oncological chronic diseases: Child-Pugh Class C liver cirrhosis, end-stage renal disease, heart failure (NYHA III or IV).
- Pregnancy.
- Previous participation in similar interventions or established active IHHT practice.
- Cognitive or linguistic barriers impairing the performance of the interventions.
- Other diseases or conditions that, in the investigator’s opinion, jeopardize patient safety or the feasibility of the study.
